summary.text: David Weprin is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 24, which he has represented since winning a special election on February 9, 2010. A Queens native, he was a New York State deputy superintendent of banks in the 1980s, worked in financial services, and served on the New York City Council, where he chaired the Finance Committee. He chairs the Assembly Insurance Committee and also serves on the Banks, Codes, Judiciary and Ways and Means committees.

paragraphs.text: Born in Queens on May 2, 1956, to Saul and Sylvia Weprin, he has lived in the Hollis-Jamaica area his entire life, according to his official Assembly biography. He graduated from Jamaica High School.
Earned a B.A. in political science (cum laude) from the State University of New York at Albany and a law degree from Hofstra University.
In 1983, Gov. Mario Cuomo named him Deputy Superintendent of Banks and Secretary of the Banking Board for New York State, a position he held through 1987.

Held leadership positions at a major financial services firm from 1987 until his election to the City Council, and was elected by his peers as Chairman of the Securities Industry Association for the New York District for three years, according to his official biography.

Elected to the New York City Council from the 23rd Council District in Queens in 2001, and became chair of its Finance Committee within weeks of taking office; Ballotpedia says he chaired the committee for eight years. He did not seek re-election in 2009 and instead ran for City Comptroller; John Liu won that office.
Won a special election on February 9, 2010 to the Assembly's 24th District, the seat previously held by his father, the late Speaker Saul Weprin, and his brother Mark Weprin.
Ran in the September 2011 special election for New York's 9th Congressional District and lost to Republican Bob Turner, according to Wikipedia.

In the Assembly, was named chair of the Committee on Correction in 2017 and earlier chaired the Task Force on People with Disabilities (2014-2016); Ballotpedia lists him as chair of the Insurance Committee in the 2025-2026 session, alongside seats on the Banks, Codes, Judiciary, and Ways and Means committees. He was named co-president of the National Association of Jewish Legislators in January 2017.

According to his official biography, he lives in Holliswood with his wife, Ronni, and has five children, and he has been affiliated with civic and community organizations including the Holliswood Civic Association and the Greater Jamaica Development Corporation.
